It sounds monotonous, which is bad for two reasons: 1) you have a high chance of getting bored of it and a higher chance of breaking and binging on junk food. 2) if you constantly eat the same, you'll be missing out on quite a bit of vitamins and minerals, which is suboptimal for health and causes more food cravings.

Try to have at least 3-4 different kind of meals that you cycle between to get more variety, like mulligatawny soup is a low-kcal chicken and veg soup with curry, rice omitted

Let's see, in addition to the chicken breast with veg on the side, you could do this mulligatawny with chicken in addition to or in place of the butternut squash (I usually skip the parsley, nigella seeds, mango chutney and yoghurt unless I happen to have them in the house, you can skip rice if you want it lower carb).

Using this recipe for chili con carne, would probably be really tasty with chicken in place, where I usually use 2x400g tins of kidney beans in chili sauce for a 4-person serving. I also use 2 tins of chopped tomatoes instead of the 1 tin of tomatoes + puree and stock. This makes it accidentally vegan, and still tasty as hell.

Lastly, there's always a good, old-fashioned stir-fry where you can add in or sub out any veggies you love/hate/have leftover.
